caption: The video showcases two hands cradling a large spherical sculpture built from polished silver magnetic balls and square magnetic tiles in patchwork clusters, against a plain light-gray backdrop. The sphere is already turning when the excerpt opens and keeps rotating slowly, sweeping different patterned faces across the frame while the background stays fixed. Bright reflective two-by-two tile clusters appear on the right and later on the left as the surface rolls, marking the steady tumble. The dark central opening shifts with the angle, a shallow depression early, a see-through gap mid-clip, partly visible at the end. The hands make small grip adjustments as they turn it, the right thumb repositioning slightly and the left contact settling higher later. Specular highlights glide across the tiles and balls as orientation changes, yet no pieces detach or get added. The rotation stays ongoing rather than completed, leaving the sphere still held and turning as the clip closes.
relations: Sphere's slow rotation sweeps patchwork tile clusters across the frame while the background stays fixed.
Hands cradling the sphere make small grip adjustments as the surface rolls beneath their contact points.
Changing viewing angle shifts the central opening from shallow depression to see-through gap and back.
Orientation changes glide specular highlights across polished balls and tiles without detaching pieces.
